title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in this 'quatrième mouture' of Analysis situs, Grothendieck builds a combinatorial theory of 'figures' and 'préfigures' in the oriented affine line M_1. These are tame or semi-linear subsets made of finitely many points and intervals, with flags (finite totally ordered sets of points or segments, Drap*) as the combinatorial data. The previous page attaches to a préfigure L its 'composed figure' Ψ = L_comp. One takes the closure, removes the isolated points, and erases redundant vertices, which gives a disjoint union of closed segments X_i = S_{a_i,b_i} with a_1<b_1<...<a_n<b_n. Then δΨ = ∂Ψ = {a_i, b_i}. To recover L from Ψ one first gives a flag (finite ordered point set) Δ ⊃ ∂Ψ: the set of all marked vertices of L.

This page sorts the vertices of Δ.
(i) Interior vertices: Δ_int = (Δ∖∂Ψ) ∩ Omb(Ψ) = Δ ∩ Omb°(Ψ), where Omb(Ψ) is the 'shadow' (the union of the closed segments) and Omb° is its interior.
(ii) Isolated vertices: Δ_is = (Δ∖∂Ψ)∖Δ_int, the marked points outside the shadow.
This gives a partition Δ = ∂Ψ ⊔ Δ_int ⊔ Δ_is.
2°) Δ_int splits further:
- Δ_red: interior vertices lying in L_0, the underlying point set. These are 'redundant' or 'gluing' vertices; removing them does not change the set.
- Δ_lac: 'lacunary' vertices, which are punctures in the interior of a segment.
So Δ_int = Δ_lac ⊔ Δ_red.
3°) Among the boundary points ∂Ψ (= ∂L) one specifies which belong to L_0 (the 'proper boundary vertices'). This is a subset ∂_0 ⊂ ∂Ψ, encoding whether each end is open or closed.

The next page states the resulting Proposition. A préfigure is determined by:
- the segment-figure Ψ, i.e. an even-length increasing sequence;
- the flag Δ ⊃ ∂Ψ;
- the subsets Δ_lac (or Δ_red) and ∂_0.
In effect this is a normal form, or bijective parametrization, of finite unions of points and intervals in a line, with marked vertices.
errors: No mathematical error. The equality (Δ∖∂Ψ)∩Omb(Ψ) = Δ∩Omb°(Ψ) holds provided Omb(Ψ) is the closed union of the segments and Omb° its interior, so that the topological boundary of Omb(Ψ) is ∂Ψ. This is true since the segments are disjoint and non-degenerate.

Δ_is as defined contains all marked points outside the shadow. Whether these must lie in L_0, i.e. whether isolated marked points not belonging to the set are allowed, is not specified on this page. A complete parametrization would need a further subset of Δ_is, analogous to ∂_0.

ideas.what: Decomposition of the vertex flag of a 1-dimensional préfigure into boundary, interior and isolated vertices, with interior vertices split into redundant and lacunary ones, plus the subset of boundary points belonging to the set.
ideas.modern_name: Normal form / cell decomposition of definable (semi-linear) subsets of R; combinatorial encoding of finite unions of points and intervals
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; o-minimal 1-dim cell decomposition (van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, 1980s)
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme announced in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), without such details

ideas.what: Recovering a préfigure from its 'composed' closed figure Ψ by adding marked points (flag Δ ⊃ ∂Ψ) and membership data.
ideas.modern_name: Stratification refinement / reduced vs marked stratifications of a 1-dimensional tame set

deep.surprise_reason: This is elementary bookkeeping: classifying finite unions of points and intervals of a line by combinatorial data. It is of interest only as a detail of Grothendieck's unpublished 1986 tame-topology foundations ('Analysis situs'). The terminology (Omb, sommets lacunaires/redondants, préfigure) is mildly notable historically, but the content is routine.
transcription_corrections: The line '[-2°) Distinguons, dans [?] donc [?],-] dans Δ_int, {+donc+} ... une décomposition en' is better read as a crossed-out '2°) Distinguons, dans Δ_int, ...' followed by 'donc une partition / une décomposition en Δ = ∂Ψ ⊔ Δ_int ⊔ Δ_is'.

In 2°), the parenthesis likely reads 'sommets intérieurs propres, ou sommets de redondance ou de raccordement' (cf. the subscript 'red'). 'les autres : Σ [?] sommets lacunaires' is likely 'les autres : sommets lacunaires'.
In 3°), the end likely reads 'i.e. on se donne une partie ∂_0 ⊂ ∂Ψ'.
Omb(Ψ) / Omb°(Ψ) = 'ombre' (shadow) of Ψ and its interior.
